subject: How to interpret the type="C2" from M2 ?

messages.author: 7b83da4f5b0156fd
messages.subject: How to interpret the type="C2" from M2 ?
parts:
Dear Dr. Chalmers, 

Thanks for the C2 function. It looks very helpful when we analyze psychometric scales with few items! However, I'm having a hard time to understand some of M2 (type = "C2") result. I have a dataset with 7 variables (It's from a depression scale). First, I ran a CFA analysis, and I got these fits.

cfa_pc <- cfa(mod_cfa_pc, data=ds_bdi_pc, estimator = 'WLSMV', ordered=names(base_bdi_pc))
fitMeasures(cfa_pc, c("aic","chisq", "df", "pvalue", "cfi", "rmsea"))
aic  chisq     df pvalue    cfi  rmsea 
NA 27.794 14.000  0.015  0.999  0.038 


Thus, I ran the graded model.
graded_pc <- mirt(ds_bdi_pc, 1, itemtype = "graded", method = "MHRM") #create the model
M2(graded_pc)
Error: M2() statistic cannot be calculated due to too few degrees of freedom

And I asked for C2.
M2(graded_pc, type="C2")
M2 df p RMSEA RMSEA_5 RMSEA_95      SRMSR       TLI CFI
stats -15.2803 14 1     0       0        0 0.03171308 -1.838626   0

Do you have any suggestion ?
Thanks.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: How to interpret the type="C2" from M2 ?
parts:
That.....is bizarre. C2 should not have returned a negative value, especially given that it's computed via a quadratic form. Could you provide a reproducible example of this (you can email code/data to me directly rather than posting it on this public forum)?

Phil

parts:
Because of my limited skills in this forum, I attach the dataset in this message and the code is the following script:

Thanks

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: How to interpret the type="C2" from M2 ?
parts:
Looks to be a particularly bad fit with respect to the covariance structure. Even SRMSR is quite high. I fit the same model with the EM algorithm (you really only need the stochastic estimators in higher dimensions) and noticed that the model did not converge after 500 cycles, which is also an indication that the data does not mold well with the select IRT models for whatever reason. 

graded_uni_fm <- mirt(fm_items,1, "graded")
M2(graded_uni_fm)
M2(graded_uni_fm, type="C2")

Phil
